articleTitle: Quantification of Acne Status Using CIELAB Color Space
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/Pacific Health Care Engineering (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Beauty industry has become one of the largest growth industries offering one of the most popular services acne treatment. Acne vulgaris is the most common skin disease in its category representing a disorder of the hair follicles and sebaceous clogged glands which lead to pimples and cysts. They can seem as plain, ordinary pimples or fluid-filled cysts that rupture and result in abscesses. They usually appear in areas where there is a high concentration of sebaceous glands, including face, chest, upper back, shoulders and neck. Acne developments is influenced by intrinsic genetics, race and hormonal factors and by extrinsic factors such as stress, diet, cosmetics and drugs. Adequate and early acne treatment focuses on preventing it from getting worse and minimizing scarring, that could last a lifetime. One of the first steps in acne treatment may involve estimation, by a dermatologist, of its density distribution of corresponding pimples and cysts. However, any form of counting and classification is a very time-consuming procedure. This motivated us to develop and test a computer aided acne detection technique.

articleTitle: Medical Equipment Design based on Risk Analysis: General Considerations
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/Pacific Health Care Engineering (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Medical equipment design, development, and manufacture are delicate processes that will result in certain level of risk involved in the use of the device. The main goal of risk analysis is to minimize hazards involved with the patient, the clinical user, and the environment. In this work, the main goal is to propose the general considerations for the design, development, and manufacture of medical equipment prototypes based on risk analysis. Several international standards are suggested to be applied. They are enforced by means of different tests for electromagnetic compatibility, electrical safety, and temperature hazards. If performed too late, a proper risk analysis may result in the re-design of parts or even the complete device. When we are aware of the risks that the prototype may be accompanied with, we can better prepare even for the tests that must be performed to prove the equipment complies with the international standards. Finally, the participation of a multidisciplinary group in all stages is highly suggested.

articleTitle: Characterization of Thermal Properties of Polymethylmethacrylate Bone Cement for Therapeutic Ultrasound Application
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/Pacific Health Care Engineering (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Biomaterials interact with biological systems and are intended to replace tissues and body organ functions. They can be classified as natural or synthetic. Polymethylmethacrylate (PMMA) is a synthetic biomaterial used, from the 1940’s to the present day, in orthopedic surgeries to replace joint surfaces and/or repair fractures. The basis of its components remains the same, small changes create variations in its properties; therefore, it is necessary to measure them. This work aims to characterize the thermal properties of PMMA, comparing them with those of soft tissues, bone and metallic prosthesis. The PMMA sample was stimulated 11 times for 3 seconds each by the modified transient plane source (MTPS), presenting the following averages: thermal conductivity =0.229± 0.006K(W/mK); effusivity =581.20± 6.22W$\mathrm{s}^{1/2}$/$\mathrm{m}^{2}$K and specific heat =1204.23± 6.88 J.kg. oC-1. The thermal properties obtained suggest that the cement would not cause local overheating, thus enabling the use of TUS on the region containing PMMA. The metallic prosthesis seems to play an important role in the dissipation of the heat generated, contributing to the non-heating of the multilayer system. However, more studies are needed to clarify this issue.

articleTitle: Piezo-Polymeric Force Sensors as an Alternate Instrumental Approach in the Tracking of Bruxism Episodes
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/Pacific Health Care Engineering (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: This paper describes the proposed application of biocompatible piezo-polymeric polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) sensors in bite force monitoring, contemplating current instrumental approaches in the assessment of brurism. This project is part of a work in progress dental exploration unit that seels to establish links between the origin and characteristic clinical patterns associated with brurism.

articleTitle: Face, Content Validity and Correlation Study of a Laparoscopic Trainer with Port Configuration Based on Quantitative aspects of Performance; Pilot Study
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/Pacific Health Care Engineering (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: The aim of this paper is to present the OpticsLTl trainer The distribution of ports and configuration was based on quantitative performance parameters such as optimal working angles, the intracorporeal-extracorporeal relationship of the instruments, the position of the surgical target and the triangulation of the instruments, among other parameters. A total of 25 surgeons participated in the different performance tests. Face and content validity was performed by laparoscopic surgeons and construct validity by medical students comparing the OpticsLT1 trainer versus the FLS trainer. OpticsLT1 trainer was successfully validated and is a useful tool to objectively evaluate the psychomotor skills of the surgeon. Its portability, ease of use, and connectivity make it practical for the didactic aspects of teaching and learning.

articleTitle: DREAMs in Cancer Cell Quiescence and Beyond
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/Pacific Health Care Engineering (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: The dimerization partner, RB-like, E2F, and multi-vulval class B (DREAM) complex is an evolutionarily conserved cell-cyclerepressive multiprotein complex and acts as a master coordinator of cell quiescence [1]. Once the DREAM complex is formed, this complex locates to the promoters of nearly a thousand cell-cycle-related genes, repressing their transcription and inducing cell quiescence. In a recent study, I reported that PAF (PCLAF/ KIAA0101) drives cell quiescence exit to promote lung tumorigenesis by remodeling the DREAM complex [2]. These results unveil one of the fundamental mechanisms of how the cancer cell bypasses cell quiescence during tumorigenesis. I am extending my research focus on DREAM-mediated cancer cell quiescence to microquiescence cancers that are closely related to cancer recurrence and metastasis.

articleTitle: Graphical interface for time and frequency patterns extraction in surface electromyography signals using Hilbert-Huang Transform.
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/Pacific Health Care Engineering (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: This paper presents the results of having developed a graphical interface in AppDesigner that allows the extraction of temporal, frequency, and those based on the Hilbert-Huang Transform features of surface electromyography signals (sEMG) of four hamstring muscles during extension of the leg. The graphical interface is useful for feature extraction of sEMG signals to identify the a subject's movement; actually, the exported feature vector that the interface yielded could be use to train a neural network for an intelligent prosthetics.

articleTitle: Measurable Assessment of Alterations Due to Face Surgery
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/Pacific Health Care Engineering (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Reconstructive surgeries have multiple purposes, sometimes they are oriented toward esthetic objectives, and in other cases are used to restore consequences of accidents and other deformities, there are not many publications addressing the degree of success of these surgical procedures or the visual transformation in these patients. The method proposed in this paper measures the degree of change between preoperative vs postoperative images based on the Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM), and they are used to compute a Probability Density Function (PDF). The results have shown to be quite successful in the measurable differentiation of the face before and after surgery, despite the challenges related to the images taken before and after the surgical procedure.

articleTitle: Nanomechanical Modeling of Viruses
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/Pacific Health Care Engineering (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: The last couple of years has motivated and triggered more in-depth research in viruses. With the recent advancement in nanotechnology and nanomechanic, the mechanical perspective of virus is an important perspective to explore. Multidisciplinary research is needed in order to gain a full understanding of how viruses work mechanically which encompasses the understanding of defect mechanics, nanomechanics, nonlinear finite element analysis, molecular dynamic and contact mechanic, just to name a few. We discuss methods for describing the physical processes underlying viral structure and self-assembly. We consider an elasticity theory and its properties in the curved space, particularly for application to obtain mechanical properties of viral capsids. We furthermore review some applications to biomechanics and nanomechanical detection of viruses. This review is aimed to spark and gain further interest in the mechanical perspective of viruses which can ultimately lead to the development of new technologies to prevent future pandemics.

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal Parameters of the Hand and Wrist in Rehabilitation using a 3D Tracking Optical Module
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/Pacific Health Care Engineering (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: The hand and wrist play a very important role in activities of daily living, and a variety of injuries can result in disability. Common treatments to recover the functions of the upper limb use physiotherapy, which is an intensive manual process, the evaluation of the progress of the patients and the performance of the rehabilitation therapy is a challenge. The objective this study is to have in the rehabilitation therapies of the affected hand and wrist there is a system to assist therapists collects data, processes and controls the movements joint during rehabilitation tasks, this data or movement spatiotemporal parameters joints can measure the joint positions hand and wrist using a 3D tracking optical module. The metacarpophalangeal (MCP) and proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joints are used to calculate movement spatiotemporal parameters joints such as angles between fingers and wrist, this data is stored in a sequence of consecutive movements. In addition, a segmentation algorithm was developed to extract the movement data for each specific joint along the axis of interest.

articleTitle: Classification of Activities of Daily Living in Subjects with Parkinson’s Disease using Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/Pacific Health Care Engineering (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Parkinson’s disease (PD) is a progressive disease characterized by slow movements, tremors, and postural instability [1]. Inertial sensors provide valuable information to assess the quality of movement in patients with PD [2]. The present work proposes improving the follow-up and support systems issued by specialists in patients with PD by identifying and adequately classifying the activities of daily living (ADL) carried out by these patients by applying programmed artificial neuronal networks (ANN) in Python language. The proposed supervised learning method allowed the classification of 6 ADLs through 64 signals from inertial sensors that made up the database (dataset) to train a multilayer perceptron (MLP), achieving an accuracy of 99%. Also, by applying dimensionality reduction to dataset, it was possible to reach 80% of accuracy in the classification. These results can potentially help the specialist to reduce costs and achieve a more accurate evaluation, seeking to improve monitoring and quality in the rehabilitation of these patients.

articleTitle: Peripheral Neuromodulation for Bionic limbs and Electroceuticals
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/Pacific Health Care Engineering (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Modulation of nerve signals in the peripheral nervous system (PNS) is a promising research field for interfacing with bionic limbs and for therapeutic applications. To achieve this, peripheral neural interfaces should be improved in terms of biocompatibility and functionality of recording and stimulation. This presentation introduces shape memory polymer neural interfaces, which have been developed for use in bionic limbs and bladder modulation. Furthermore, this paper introduces triboelectric neurostimulators for modulating peripheral nerves.

articleTitle: Portable Humidity Measurement System in Eyeball Models Based on a PVDF Membrane Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/Pacific Health Care Engineering (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Throughout this manuscript it is described how the humidity dependent capacitance of a polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) membrane was leveraged as a principle of a humidity measurement system in models of eyeball, subjected to realistic intraocular pressures (IOP) and exposed to artificial tears. The membrane, and its electrical terminals, were attached to a contact lens, and subsequently, connected to a capacitance-voltage converter circuit. In addition, the voltage response was digitally recorded in a micro-SD card with minimal operator intervention. The entire system was constructed and fixed in a commercial helmet and is energized by rechargeable battery. The voltage output of the system is dependent on IOP and artificial tear volume (ATV).

articleTitle: Design and Construction of a Mechanical Model of Thorax
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/Pacific Health Care Engineering (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: This article presents the results of the investigation in progress, about a device designed to simulate the thoracic region for ultrasonic inspection purposes. It is oriented to simulate healthy cases and conditions as well as cases with illnesses. Focused on pleural effusion that occurs when the pleural membranes separate because of different causes, although it should be noted that the device could simulate another ailment. Different pathologies can cause pleural effusion and, since the pleural cavity is an area of difficult access, it is necessary to take preventive measures preventing harming the patient and avoiding risky processes such as thoracocentesis or biopsies, being able to obtain rapid diagnoses to reduce the risk. The system comprises two essential parts, the first where a phantom of muscle and pleura is coupled to simulate the thoracic cavity and the second, the movement mechanism that simulates the separation of the pleural membranes. As a result, a portable, light, and a suitable device was obtained to perform ultrasonic analysis with a resolution of 0.01mm.

articleTitle: A BI-RADS-based Approach for Tumor Classification in Breast Ultrasound Using Binary Decomposition Strategies
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/Pacific Health Care Engineering (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: This article presents a BI-RADS-based method for classifying breast tumors on ultrasound. The multiclass classification problem into BI-RADS categories 2 to 5 is addressed by two binary decomposition schemes: one-vs.-all (OVA) and one-vs.-one (OVO). Furthermore, the base classifiers of these strategies are trained with local features that are selected using a search method based on the genetic algorithm. The experimental results show that the proposed approach outperforms the classification performance of traditional OVO and OVA approaches that use a global feature space shared by all base classifiers. Therefore, using local features allows the specialization of the base classifiers to distinguish between two specific classes.

articleTitle: Development of an Electrical Pulse Generator based on a BaTiO3 Piezoelectric Ceramic with Pt Implant for Tissue Stimulation.
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/Pacific Health Care Engineering (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Smart materials are one of the most promising technologies with a great potential today, these materials can represent new solutions to multiple areas of technological development [1]. Some materials, such as piezoelectric, have been used as actuators, control tools, information processing, sensing, integrating them into electrical and electronic systems for a wide range of applications [2,3]. This work focuses on the implementation of BaTiO<inf>3</inf> ceramics with Pt implant in an electrical system capable of generating periodic pulses in order to use them for tissue stimulation.

articleTitle: Technological Maturity Classification, Focus: Medical Devices
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/Pacific Health Care Engineering (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Investment in science and technology oriented to the health sector have been affected by the appearance of misinformation and the massive use of collaborative tools found on the Internet that provide subjective or dubious information on the development of new medical technologies in Mexico. These new products do not take into account the monitoring of a maturation stage nor do they comply with the necessary regulations for the product to comply with for optimal development in the industry. This article focuses on emphasizing the importance of the classification of technological maturity and steps to be fulfilled for each stage, focusing on essential characteristics of the health sector, the case in Mexico is discussed.

articleTitle: Characterization of Electromagnetic Field Intensity Through Random Distributions of Bubbles Induced by Acoustic Cavitation
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/Pacific Health Care Engineering (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Acoustic cavitation is a complex phenomenon to study and model due to the effects it produces in liquid media, mainly the generation of bubbles. Among the complexities are the number of bubbles generated, their location, and their size. For this reason, it is proposed to use an optical medium such as light in the form of an electromagnetic field to quantify the level of cavitation present in a liquid medium. For this, a model is required to represent what happens when cavitation is generated, so first, a matrix that randomly represented the complex parameters of the bubbles generated by cavitation (quantity, size, and position) was programmed. In this model the study of the intensity of the electromagnetic field through a medium with water and bubbles in different random distributions was performed. Analyzing the relationship found between the reduction in the intensity of an electromagnetic field because the reflection, refraction, and absorption of the waves with cavitation randomly induced bubbles, regardless of their diminished size it was found a reduction in the field intensity of 5.03% and 6.87% depending on the size and number of bubbles generated. This study was the first step to approach a new optical technique to quantify the level of acoustic cavitation.

articleTitle: Tool for Semi-Automatic Segmentation and Labeling of Regions of Interest on Mid-Lateral Oblique Screen-Film Mammograms
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/Pacific Health Care Engineering (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) algorithms have enormous potential applications and cover the entire medical imaging lifecycle, from image creation, diagnosis, classification and even prediction of particular pathologies. A problem for the development and clinical application of AI algorithms is the limited availability of extensive and representative training data including expert labeling (Manual Labeling). Current supervised AI methods require a data pre-processing stage for labeling data to train, validate and test algorithms with an optimal approximation to the ground truth. In this paper, a graphical interface was developed and implemented to label in a semi-automatic way Regions of Interest of Mid-Middle Lateral Oblique Screen-Film Mammography (MMLOSFM) through pre-processing techniques such as segmentation and image enhancement. Based on the analysis performed using four structural comparison indexes, it was demonstrated an efficient segmentation and labeling of MMLOSFM with a consistently high similarity (91.6% compared to the ground truth provided by the MIAS database).

articleTitle: Design Proposition: Medium Power Ultrasonic Generator for Bone Consolidation Therapy
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/Pacific Health Care Engineering (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Ultrasound (US) has several applications in medicine, including: therapeutic, surgical and diagnostic procedures. The use for therapeutic purposes has had a wide impact and application at an international level. The emission of medium power US is essential for the rapid recovery of patients who present deficiencies in the bone consolidation process. This article proposes the design proposal of a Medium Power Ultrasonic Generator for therapeutic purposes, a rapid recovery will be promoted when there are deficiencies in this process, avoiding surgical procedures and their subsequent associated complications, offering a better quality of life to this sector. so sensitive and vulnerable of society. The proposed equipment has been developed by this research group in a multilateral project financed by MESCYT. The equipment achieved is portable, low-cost, robust, and easy to use.

articleTitle: Semiconductor-based Bio Sensor for Digital Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/Pacific Health Care Engineering (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: Semiconductor-based biosensor is important for the digital healthcare technology which is changing a healthcare paradigm from the hospital to the personal area. By combining a digital-biosensor with a microfluidic technology and automated mobile diagnosis system, peoples can monitor their body conditions in real-time themselves and thus prevent serious illnesses. In this presentation, semiconductor-based biosensors, disposable microfluidic device, and automated systems of the National NanoFab Center are introduced.

articleTitle: Mechanism that Emulates the Flexible Endoscope for Training: A Proof of Concept
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/Pacific Health Care Engineering (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: the aim of this work is to present the initial prototype of a proof of concept of a system that emulates the flexible endoscope, the system was modeled in Solid Works and printed in 3D for its elaboration. The development and initial tests to which it was subjected are shown. The design of the flexible endoscope has a potential to be tested in navigation training tasks and visuospatial adaptation.

articleTitle: Bioelectronic Stress Hormone Monitoring Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/Pacific Health Care Engineering (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: In this presentation, semiconductor-based biosensor platform for a detection of stress hormone, i.e. cortisol, is introduced for futuristic applications at an era with internet of things (IoT). Basically, cortisol monoclonal antibody (c-Mab) or cortisol specific aptamer are chemically tethered on semiconductor surface for the cortisol detection by its specific biological binding with the bioelectronic sensor. Its principle and futuristic platform will be introduced and discussed for a monitoring of psychic biomarker.

articleTitle: Contrast Enhancement of 3D X-ray Microtomography Using CLAHE for Trabecular Bone Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/Pacific Health Care Engineering (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: X-ray microtomography $(\mu \mathrm{CT})$ is a nondestructive and high-resolution method of microstructural analysis. The $\mu C T$ is compounded by a succession of 2D grayscale digital images, in this work a three stages methodology is proposed to enhance these images: image acquisition, image processing, and image post-processing. In the image processing stage an image integration, an anisotropic diffusion filter, the CLAHE algorithm, a morphological reconstruction, and a segmentation with the OTSU method are applied. SSIM is used to measure the structural similarity between the image after the CLAHE and the image next to the morphological reconstruction. This is used to determine a disk as a structural element with a radius of 1, with these values in the morphological reconstruction, SSIM greater than 0.95 is achieved. Another comparison is made between the original $\mu \mathrm{CT}$ image and the image after the morphological reconstruction to measure the similarity, obtaining an SSIM greater than 0.90. This index is used to determine the clip value for the CLAHE, the clip range is 0.085 - 0.1. After the application of the proposed methodology, the results are compared using the Jaccard index obtaining a value greater than 0.90. The segmented images can be used to obtain bone morphometry and know the bone quality.

articleTitle: Radial Arterial Pulse Simulation System in Three Modalities for Teaching Purposes According to Traditional Chinese Medicine
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/Pacific Health Care Engineering (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: The diagnosis of the radial arterial pulse is used in Traditional Chinese Medicine as a clinical procedure that allows knowing the state of health of a person or organ holistically based on the specialist's sensitivity, knowledge, and experience. To perform this task, people interested in practicing pulsology require extensive training. The present work consists of a simulator development of the blood pulse of the radial artery in three complementary modalities. According to the practice of traditional Chinese medicine, this proposal allows students and medical doctors to become familiar with the pulse by feeling, observing, and listening, associating the information with medical diagnoses. For these purposes, the radial arterial pulse signal is applied to an electromechanical actuator for the pressure modality, a display for graph presentation, and the reproduction as audio derived from the harmonics generated by a speaker. In this way, those students and specialists interested in traditional Chinese medicine could identify the blood pulse parameters in less time than those using only pressure-based systems. Due to the lack of databases related to radial pulse signals, pulse graphic models reported were quantified and concatenated to generate and reproduce the pulse signals continuously. The system was designed around the STM32F4Discovery development card for quantization, digitizing, and reproducing the pulse signal through algorithms implemented in the programming platform of the card processor. The pulse signal is applied to a linear voice coil motor, a speaker as a transducer, and a graphic display. The proposal, through three modalities, contributes to studies of pulse signals for a possible reduction of training time in the learning process.

articleTitle: Case Studies of Mental Problems in South Korea and India: Why Knowing the National Demographics First Helps Choose Better Medical Technical Interventions
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/Pacific Health Care Engineering (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: To improve Information Communication Technology for Development (ICT4D) in e-health applications means getting maximum advantage at minimum cost to purveyors and consumers. This is a conceptual and empirical paper arguing three kinds of data are important to know beforehand to create informed decisions to maximize beneficial uses of online technology to aid mental health: (1) how do you define the etiology of mental health problems; (2) how do you define who should be helped as a priority, and (3) how do you make decisions technically to fit the former two points? Since serving patients is more important than technical profiteering, these three critical decision points mean primary medical choices of diagnosis and secondary national demographic research should guide a more conditioned tertiary technical use, instead of vice versa that regularly leads to cutting patients to fit pre-determined and misaligned technological investments. Two case studies of this technical vetting procedure are summarized on the mental health demographics of South Korea and India. It should influence the current state of the art for how to reach patients best via Internet-connected technologies for monitoring and treating depression. Policy advice on platform design is better once this vetting procedure is used.

articleTitle: Oriented Dialogue Added to Virtual Reality Resources: An Application of the Holographic Model in the Treatment of Parkinson’s Disease
publicationTitle: 2023 Global Medical Engineering Physics Exchanges/Pacific Health Care Engineering (GMEPE/PAHCE)
abstract: The present study tested the Oriented Dialogue (OD) technique added to virtual reality (VR) resources in a treatment of Parkinson’s disease. Originally, OD consists of the patient mind conditioning through a specific dialog, performed by the physician in charge of the treatment, which gives a new consciousness to the patients about their disease, contributing to cerebral neuroplasticity increasing and consequently to symptoms’ relief. Currently, OD is part of a short video which allows the patients to experiment an immersion inside of knowledge about their diseases and teaches them how to make the dialog for each case. The patients usually use a VR headset, but video can be showed in a television for those who do not feel comfortable with 3D effects. For the present case of Parkinson’s disease, a 36-year-old woman with severe tremor symptoms, vocal hypotonia, and inability to perform fine movements – such as doing nails, writing, and change facial expression – was treated by a multidisciplinary team, including general practitioner, speech therapist, neurologist, orthopedist, and physiotherapist. In addition to the conventional protocols, the professionals used the combination OD/VR during medical appointments and oriented the patient to daily repeat the technique at home. After 90 days, the patient reported improvement of 90% of the symptoms.
